q1_issues.issue: The bare mass-kind subject 'Salt-bloom' is used as a role filler in a single flat event, where a verbal generic over a kind is prescribed as an Implication rule over instances (bare class symbols are licensed only as non-specific objects).

q2_gaps: perception verb whose SUBJECT is the perceived source rather than a perceiver ('X smells/tastes/looks of Y'): the role table lists see/hear under Experiencer for the perceiver and reserves Stimulus for the percept, leaving the emitter subject undetermined — the stative-intransitive default lands it on Experiencer, which names the wrong participant

intensity adverb on a verb ('faintly') falls between the barred 'degree adverb on a verb' class (sharply / slightly — no licensed slot, leave out and record the gap) and the licensed Manner class, whose own exemplar 'brightly' is itself an intensity adverb; no test separates them
notes: The compound genus (Inheritance salt_bloom bloom) with the noun modifier unexposed and the bare-mass oblique object (Of sk_smell_1 salt) both follow doctrine.
